question: Which committee recommended the formation of a new category of NBFC i.e., Non-Banking Financial Company-Micro Finance Institution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malegam Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Malegam Committee, headed by Y.H. Malegam, was constituted by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 2010 to study the issues in the microfinance sector. (मालेगाम समिति — एनबीएफसी-एमएफआई)

 

• It recommended the creation of a new category of NBFC called NBFC-MFI (Non-Banking Financial Company-Micro Finance Institution) so that microfinance institutions could be regulated separately from other NBFCs.

 

• The committee submitted its report in January 2011, and its recommendations — including caps on lending rates and margins — formed the basis of the RBI's regulatory framework for NBFC-MFIs notified later in 2011.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Malegam Committee also recommended that not more than two MFIs should lend to the same borrower and prescribed a minimum net-worth requirement for NBFC-MFIs.

 

NOTE

 

• Shah Committee (Option 1): This name refers to other RBI/government panels and is not linked to the creation of the NBFC-MFI category.

 

• Kamath Committee (Option 3): The K.V. Kamath Committee (2020) recommended sector-specific financial parameters for the one-time restructuring of Covid-19-stressed loans, an unrelated matter.

 

• Hussain Committee (Option 4): Not associated with the NBFC-MFI classification.

question: Harrod Domar growth model is known for highlighting the role of savings and investments. Which Five-Year Plan in India was based on this model?
solution_text:
The correct answer is First.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model, which links the rate of economic growth to the level of savings and productivity of capital investment. (हैरोड-डोमर मॉडल — प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• The plan focused mainly on agriculture, irrigation and power projects, including river valley projects like the Bhakra Nangal Dam, and it succeeded in achieving a growth rate higher than its target.

 

• The Harrod-Domar model essentially argues that an economy needs to save and invest a certain proportion of its national income simply to make up for wear-and-tear of capital and to achieve additional growth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61) was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis model, which emphasised rapid industrialisation with a focus on heavy and basic industries.

 

• The Fourth Plan (1969-74) adopted the objective of "Growth with Stability" and included the Gadgil formula for resource allocation to states.

 

NOTE

 

• Second (Option 2): Based on the Mahalanobis model, not the Harrod-Domar model.

 

• Fourth (Option 3) and Third (Option 4): Neither of these plans was based on the Harrod-Domar model; the Third Plan (1961-66) aimed at making the economy self-reliant.

question: Fundamental duties are ___________ and not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is statutory.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens are listed in Part IVA, Article 51A of the Constitution. They are described as statutory duties and are not enforceable by law, but courts do take them into account while adjudicating matters. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• They were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and were inspired by Article 59 of the erstwhile USSR Constitution.

 

• Originally there were 10 Fundamental Duties; an 11th duty (a parent/guardian's duty to provide educational opportunities to children aged 6-14) was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning no citizen can be directly punished by a court for their violation, though courts may refer to them for guidance.

 

• Fundamental Duties apply only to citizens of India, unlike Fundamental Rights, some of which extend to non-citizens as well.

 

NOTE

 

• regulatory (Option 1): Not the term used in constitutional literature to describe Fundamental Duties.

 

• non-statutory (Option 2): Incorrect — Fundamental Duties are described as statutory in nature, not non-statutory.

 

• common (Option 4): Not a recognised classification for Fundamental Duties.

question: When did Dmitri Mendeleev invent the periodic table, ordering the symbols of the chemical elements according to their atomic weights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1869.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev published his first version of the periodic table of chemical elements in 1869, arranging elements in order of increasing atomic weight. (आवर्त सारणी — दिमित्री मेंडेलीव, 1869)

 

• Mendeleev's table left gaps for elements that were not yet discovered and successfully predicted the properties of undiscovered elements such as gallium, scandium and germanium.

 

• The modern periodic table is now arranged by atomic number (proposed later by Henry Moseley in 1913) rather than atomic weight.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• German chemist Lothar Meyer independently developed a similar periodic arrangement of elements around the same time as Mendeleev.

 

• Mendeleev is often called the "Father of the Periodic Table", and element 101 (Mendelevium) is named in his honour.

 

NOTE

 

• 1794, 1890 and 1779 (Options 1, 3 and 4): None of these years correspond to Mendeleev's publication of the periodic table; 1869 is the historically correct year.

question: The FIFA World Cup 2026 will be hosted by _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Canada, USA and Mexico.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The FIFA World Cup 2026 will be jointly hosted by Canada, the United States and Mexico, making it the first World Cup to be hosted by three countries. (फीफा विश्व कप 2026 — कनाडा, अमेरिका और मेक्सिको)

 

• It will be the first FIFA World Cup with 48 teams, expanded from the earlier 32-team format.

 

• Mexico will thus become the first country to host the men's FIFA World Cup three times (after 1970 and 1986).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Matches of the 2026 World Cup will be played across 16 host cities spread across the three co-host nations.

 

• The FIFA World Cup 2022 was hosted by Qatar, and it was the first World Cup held in the Arab world.

 

NOTE

 

• Canada, USA and Brazil (Option 2), Argentina, Brazil and USA (Option 3) and USA, Brazil and Chili (Option 4): These combinations are incorrect; Brazil and Argentina are not co-hosts of the 2026 World Cup — the confirmed hosts are Canada, USA and Mexico.

question: Ethanoic acid is a synonym for which acidic liquid is used in kitchens around the world as a basic seasoning in the preparation and cooking of certain foods?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinegar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethanoic acid, also known as acetic acid (CH₃COOH), is the main component of vinegar, typically present in a concentration of about 4-8%. (एथेनोइक अम्ल — सिरका/विनेगर)

 

• Vinegar is widely used in kitchens as a seasoning, preservative and pickling agent due to the sour taste and preservative properties of acetic acid.

 

• Ethanoic acid is produced industrially and also naturally through the fermentation of ethanol by acetic acid bacteria.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Glacial acetic acid refers to pure, water-free acetic acid, which freezes just below room temperature (16.6°C) into ice-like crystals, giving it the name "glacial".

 

• Common household vinegar (white vinegar) is essentially a dilute solution of acetic acid in water.

 

NOTE

 

• Apple Juice (Option 1): A fruit juice, not an acid used as a seasoning; apple cider vinegar (made from fermented apple juice) contains acetic acid, but apple juice itself does not.

 

• Vanillin (Option 2): The primary compound giving vanilla its flavour and aroma, unrelated to ethanoic acid.

 

• Caustic Soda (Option 3): This is sodium hydroxide (NaOH), a strong base/alkali, not an acid.

question: Who among the following devised a policy that came to be known as the Doctrine of Lapse?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Dalhousie.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856, devised and implemented the Doctrine of Lapse. (हड़प नीति — लॉर्ड डलहौजी)

 

• Under this policy, if an Indian ruler died without a natural male heir, his state would be annexed ('lapse') to the British East India Company, and an adopted heir would not be recognised as the legitimate ruler.

 

• States annexed under this doctrine include Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Dalhousie is also credited with laying the foundation of the railways, telegraph and postal system in India, and with introducing administrative reforms.

 

• The annexation of Awadh (Oudh) in 1856 by Dalhousie on grounds of misgovernance (not through the Doctrine of Lapse) was a major cause of resentment leading to the Revolt of 1857.

 

NOTE

 

• The Lord Ellenborough (Option 1): Governor-General from 1842-44, known for the annexation of Sindh.

 

• Lord William Bentinck (Option 2): Known for social reforms such as the abolition of Sati (1829) and suppression of Thuggee.

 

• Lord Canning (Option 4): The last Governor-General and first Viceroy of India; he was in office during the Revolt of 1857.

question: Sonal Mansingh, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan awardee, is an accomplished dancer of which of the following dances in addition to the Bharatanatyam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sonal Mansingh is a renowned Indian classical dancer, choreographer and guru, celebrated for her mastery of both Bharatanatyam and Odissi. (सोनल मानसिंह — ओडिसी नृत्यांगना)

 

• She has been honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1992) and the Padma Vibhushan (2003), among India's highest civilian awards.

 

• She is also a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and has served as a nominated Member of the Rajya Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sonal Mansingh founded the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CID) in New Delhi to promote and train students in classical dance forms.

 

• Other prominent Odissi exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sanjukta Panigrahi and Madhavi Mudgal.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 1): A classical dance-drama form of Kerala, not associated with Sonal Mansingh.

 

• Kathak (Option 2): A classical dance form of North India, unrelated to Sonal Mansingh's primary repertoire.

 

• Sattriya (Option 3): A classical dance form of Assam, originating in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras), not associated with Sonal Mansingh.

question: In which of the following cities is the Quwwat al-Islam mosque situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque is located in the Qutub complex, Mehrauli, Delhi, adjacent to the Qutub Minar. (कुव्वत-उल-इस्लाम मस्जिद — दिल्ली)

 

• It was built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1193 CE, and is considered the first mosque built in India by the rulers of the Delhi Sultanate.

 

• The mosque was constructed using materials salvaged from demolished Hindu and Jain temples, and its name translates to "Might of Islam".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Qutub Minar, begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by his successor Iltutmish, stands within the same complex and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• The Iron Pillar in the Qutub complex, dating to the Gupta period, is famous for its rust-resistant composition.

 

NOTE

 

• Panipat (Option 1): Famous for the three historic Battles of Panipat, not for the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque.

 

• Lahore (Option 2): Located in present-day Pakistan; known for the Badshahi Mosque, not Quwwat-ul-Islam.

 

• Ajmer (Option 3): Known for the Dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti and the Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra mosque, not Quwwat-ul-Islam.

question: 'Mati-Akhora' is associated with which of the following classical dances of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mati-Akhora refers to a set of fundamental exercises and body movements performed on the ground as basic training in Sattriya dance. (माटी-आखरा — सत्रिया नृत्य, असम)

 

• Sattriya is a classical dance form that originated in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) of Assam, founded by the saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva in the 15th century.

 

• It was accorded the status of a classical dance form of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sattriya was traditionally performed by bhokots (monks) in the sattras as a part of religious rituals, and later evolved to include female performers on stage.

 

• India recognises eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 1): A classical dance form of Odisha, not associated with Mati-Akhora.

 

• Kathakali (Option 2): A classical dance-drama of Kerala, unrelated to Mati-Akhora.

 

• Kathak (Option 4): A classical dance form of North India, unrelated to Mati-Akhora.

question: Which of the following schemes is available to people in the age group of 18 to 50 years and provides risk coverage of ₹2 lakh in case of death of the insured, due to any reason, at an annual premium of ₹436?
option_1: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJY)
option_3: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-SYM)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJY).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), launched in 2015, is a life insurance scheme offering a cover of ₹2 lakh in case of death of the insured due to any reason. (प्रधानमंत्री जीवन ज्योति बीमा योजना — ₹2 लाख जीवन बीमा)

 

• It is available to people in the 18-50 years age group with a bank/post office account, and the annual premium was revised from ₹330 to ₹436 with effect from 1 June 2022.

 

• The scheme is a one-year renewable term life insurance policy, administered through participating banks and life insurance companies including LIC.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Both PMJJBY and PMSBY were launched together on 9 May 2015 in Kolkata by the Prime Minister, as part of the government's financial inclusion and social security initiatives.

 

• PMJJBY covers death due to any cause, whereas PMSBY (below) is specifically an accident insurance scheme.

 

NOTE

 

• Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (Option 2): An accidental death and disability insurance scheme offering ₹2 lakh cover for accidental death/full disability at a premium of ₹20 (later revised to ₹20) per year — it does not cover death due to any reason.

 

• Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan Yojana (Option 3): A pension scheme for unorganised sector workers, not a life insurance scheme.

 

• Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (Option 4): A pension scheme for senior citizens (aged 60 and above), not a life insurance scheme for the 18-50 age group.

question: Chittaranjan Das along with ________ set up the Swaraj Party in 1923 to contest the elections.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Motilal Nehru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swaraj Party was founded in 1923 by Chittaranjan (C.R.) Das and Motilal Nehru. (स्वराज पार्टी — चितरंजन दास और मोतीलाल नेहरू)

 

• It was formed after the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922 (following the Chauri Chaura incident), by leaders who wanted to contest council elections and oppose the British from within the legislatures.

 

• C.R. Das served as the party's President and Motilal Nehru as its Secretary; the party contested and won a number of seats in the Central Legislative Assembly elections of 1923.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Swaraj Party's strategy of contesting elections and obstructing government business from inside the councils was known as the "Council Entry" or "Obstructionist" programme.

 

• Motilal Nehru was also the father of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, and twice served as President of the Indian National Congress.

 

NOTE

 

• Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 1): Known as the "Iron Man of India"; led the Bardoli Satyagraha and later integrated the princely states, not a co-founder of the Swaraj Party.

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 2): Later became the first President of India; not a co-founder of the Swaraj Party.

 

• Jawahar Lal Nehru (Option 4): Son of Motilal Nehru; not the co-founder of the Swaraj Party (Motilal was).

question: Who among the following became the first Indian to be invited to perform at the prestigious Lincoln Centre Hall in the United States of America?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bismillah Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan, the legendary shehnai maestro, became the first Indian to be invited to perform at the prestigious Lincoln Center Hall in the United States of America. (बिस्मिल्लाह खान — शहनाई वादक)

 

• He is widely credited with popularising the shehnai as a classical solo concert instrument, elevating it from a purely ceremonial instrument.

 

• He was honoured with India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, in 2001, becoming only the third classical musician to receive it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bismillah Khan famously performed at India's first Independence Day celebration at the Red Fort on 15 August 1947, and again on the eve of India's 50th year of independence in 1997.

 

• He was also awarded the Padma Vibhushan (1980) and the Padma Bhushan (1968) earlier in his career.

 

NOTE

 

• M.S. Subbalakshmi (Option 1): A legendary Carnatic vocalist and the first Indian musician to receive the Bharat Ratna (1998); she was famed for performing at the UN General Assembly, not for being first at Lincoln Center.

 

• Zakir Hussain (Option 2): A world-renowned tabla player; not the first Indian invited to Lincoln Center.

 

• Ravi Shankar (Option 3): A globally celebrated sitar maestro who popularised Indian classical music in the West; not credited as the first Indian at Lincoln Center.

question: Identify the sealed glass vacuum tube containing an electron beam that is focused on a phosphor-coated glass screen when light is emitted.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cathode ray tube.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) is a sealed glass vacuum tube containing an electron gun that produces a focused beam of electrons directed at a phosphor-coated screen, which emits light where the beam strikes it. (कैथोड रे ट्यूब — पुराने टीवी और मॉनिटर)

 

• CRTs were the primary display technology used in older television sets, computer monitors and oscilloscopes before the advent of flat-panel displays.

 

• The technology is based on the principle of thermionic emission and electron deflection using magnetic or electric fields to scan the beam across the screen line by line.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CRT was invented based on work by Karl Ferdinand Braun in 1897, and it was long known as the "Braun tube".

 

• CRTs have largely been replaced by LCD, LED and plasma displays, which are thinner, lighter and more energy-efficient.

 

NOTE

 

• Flat array tube (Option 2): Not a standard recognised display technology term matching this description.

 

• Light Emitting Diode tube (Option 3): LED displays use semiconductor diodes to emit light directly, not an electron beam striking a phosphor screen.

 

• Liquid Crystal Display tube (Option 4): LCDs work by manipulating liquid crystals with polarised light, not by firing an electron beam at a phosphor screen.

question: Which is the oldest aluminium refinery plant in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Muri Alumina Plant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Muri Alumina Plant, located in Muri, Ramgarh district, Jharkhand, is the oldest aluminium refinery/plant in India, established in 1943 by the Indian Aluminium Company (Indal). (मुरी एल्युमिना संयंत्र — भारत का सबसे पुराना एल्युमिनियम रिफाइनरी)

 

• It has been operating for over eight decades and is currently owned by Hindalco Industries.

 

• Muri combines both an alumina refinery and an aluminium smelter at the same location.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Damanjodi Plant in Odisha is operated by NALCO (National Aluminium Company) and is one of the largest alumina refineries in Asia, but it is much newer than Muri (commissioned in the 1980s).

 

• India is among the world's top producers of bauxite and aluminium, with major refineries also located in Odisha and Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• The Damanjodi Plant (Option 1): A large modern NALCO refinery in Odisha, not the oldest.

 

• The Mettur Plant (Option 3): Known for the Mettur Dam in Tamil Nadu; not the oldest aluminium refinery.

 

• The Belgaum Plant (Option 4): Located in Karnataka; not the oldest aluminium refinery in India.

question: The Rajgir Zoo is located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rajgir Zoo Safari is located in Rajgir, Nalanda district, Bihar. (राजगीर चिड़ियाघर सफारी — बिहार)

 

• Inaugurated in 2016, it is notable as India's first zoo safari to house both herbivore and carnivore safaris (including tiger, lion, bear and leopard safaris) within a single complex spread across the Rajgir hills.

 

• Rajgir is also historically significant as an ancient capital of the Magadha kingdom and an important centre for Buddhism and Jainism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other attractions near Rajgir include the Nalanda University ruins, the Vishwa Shanti Stupa (World Peace Pagoda) and the ancient Cyclopean Wall.

 

• Bihar is also home to the Valmiki Tiger Reserve, one of India's key tiger conservation areas.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Home to zoos such as Arignar Anna Zoological Park, Chennai, not the Rajgir Zoo.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Known for Van Vihar National Park and several tiger reserves, not the Rajgir Zoo.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): Home to the Sakkarbaug Zoo, not the Rajgir Zoo.

question: The word 'direct free kick' is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Football.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A direct free kick is a term used in football (soccer), awarded to a team when the opposing team commits certain fouls, such as kicking, tripping, pushing or handling the ball deliberately. (डायरेक्ट फ्री किक — फुटबॉल)

 

• A goal can be scored directly from a direct free kick without the ball needing to touch another player first, unlike an indirect free kick.

 

• Free kicks are a key part of the Laws of the Game framed by the International Football Association Board (IFAB).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FIFA World Cup, football's premier international tournament, is organised by FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association), headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland.

 

• Famous free-kick specialists in football history include players like David Beckham, Roberto Carlos and Lionel Messi.

 

NOTE

 

• Basketball (Option 1): Uses terms like free throw and foul shot, not "direct free kick".

 

• Baseball (Option 2): Uses terms such as strike, ball and home run, unrelated to free kicks.

 

• Volleyball (Option 3): Uses terms such as serve, spike and block, not free kicks.

question: 'Padhe Bharat' reading campaign, launched by the Department of School Education and Literacy to support and encourage children to read for a joyful learning experience started on January 1, 2022, for a period of ________ days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 100.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Padhe Bharat' reading campaign, launched by the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, was rolled out as a 100-days reading campaign starting 1 January 2022. (पढ़े भारत अभियान — 100 दिन का पठन अभियान)

 

• It was launched by Union Education Minister Shri Dharmendra Pradhan, aiming to encourage students to read for joy and to build lifelong reading habits.

 

• The campaign encouraged students to prepare a reading list and share their reading experiences, and involved teachers, parents and the community.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'Padhe Bharat' complements the goals of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which emphasises foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) for all children by Grade 3.

 

• The Ministry of Education also runs the NIPUN Bharat Mission to achieve universal foundational literacy and numeracy by 2026-27.

 

NOTE

 

• 200, 50 and 150 (Options 2, 3 and 4): These durations are incorrect; the officially announced duration of the Padhe Bharat campaign was 100 days.

question: 'Swachh Bharat Mission' is associated with which public figure?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swachh Bharat Mission (Clean India Mission) was launched on 2 October 2014, deliberately chosen to coincide with the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, to fulfil his long-cherished vision of a clean India. (स्वच्छ भारत मिशन — महात्मा गांधी की जयंती)

 

• Gandhi had emphasised sanitation and cleanliness as being as important as independence itself, famously stating that "sanitation is more important than independence."

 

• The mission aimed to achieve an Open Defecation Free (ODF) India and to improve solid waste management across urban and rural India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The mission has two sub-missions: Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) for rural areas, run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, and Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban), run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

 

• India was declared Open Defecation Free (ODF) on 2 October 2019, marking the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Lal Bahadur Shastri (Options 2, 3 and 4): While all are important national leaders, the Swachh Bharat Mission is specifically associated with fulfilling Mahatma Gandhi's vision of sanitation and cleanliness.

question: In December 2021, the ________ approved a $500 million loan to the Government of India to help improve the quality of the country's school education and mitigate the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on the students' learning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asian Development Bank.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In December 2021, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) approved a $500 million loan to the Government of India under the "Supporting Human Capital Development in School Education Program". (एशियाई विकास बैंक — $500 मिलियन ऋण)

 

• The loan aimed to help improve the quality of school education in India and to mitigate the learning losses caused by the Covid-19 pandemic.

 

• ADB, headquartered in Manila, Philippines, is a regional development bank that provides financial and technical assistance to developing member countries in Asia and the Pacific.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• ADB was established in 1966 and India has been a founding member since its inception.

 

• ADB has funded numerous infrastructure and social sector projects in India, spanning urban development, transport and education.

 

NOTE

 

• Central Bank of Bahrain (Option 1): The central bank/monetary authority of Bahrain, not involved in this loan.

 

• European Central Bank (Option 2): The central bank for the Eurozone, unrelated to this India-specific loan.

 

• National Development Bank (Option 4): Not the institution that approved this loan; it is not a globally recognised multilateral lender in this context.

question: Till which year did the High Court of Delhi continue to exercise jurisdiction over Himachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1971.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The High Court of Delhi continued to exercise jurisdiction over Himachal Pradesh until 1971. (दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय — हिमाचल प्रदेश उच्च न्यायालय, 1971)

 

• A separate Himachal Pradesh High Court was established under the Himachal Pradesh High Court Act, 1971, and it came into existence on 25 January 1971, taking over jurisdiction from the Delhi High Court.

 

• Himachal Pradesh attained full statehood on 25 January 1971, the same date its High Court was established.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Delhi High Court itself was established under the Delhi High Court Act, 1966, and at different times exercised jurisdiction over neighbouring union territories, including Himachal Pradesh, before their own High Courts were set up.

 

• The seat of the Himachal Pradesh High Court is in Shimla.

 

NOTE

 

• 1969, 1967 and 1968 (Options 1, 2 and 4): These years are incorrect; the Delhi High Court's jurisdiction over Himachal Pradesh formally ended in 1971, when the Himachal Pradesh High Court was established.

question: Which ecologist is famous for studying plant life in the Indiana Dunes in 1896?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Henry Chandler Cowles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Henry Chandler Cowles, an American botanist/ecologist, is famous for his pioneering studies of plant life and ecological succession on the Indiana Dunes along Lake Michigan, beginning in the 1890s. (हेनरी चांडलर काउल्स — पादप अनुक्रमण अध्ययन)

 

• His research, published in 1899 as "The Ecological Relations of the Vegetation on the Sand Dunes of Lake Michigan", is considered a founding work of plant ecology and the study of ecological succession.

 

• Cowles is often referred to as the "Father of American Plant Ecology" (or of "dynamic ecology") for showing how plant communities change progressively over time on the shifting dunes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indiana Dunes area, where Cowles conducted his studies, is now protected as the Indiana Dunes National Park.

 

• Cowles taught at the University of Chicago, which became an early hub for the emerging field of plant ecology in the United States.

 

NOTE

 

• Robert MacArthur (Option 1): A prominent ecologist known for work on island biogeography (with E.O. Wilson) and species niche theory, not the Indiana Dunes studies.

 

• G Evelyn Hutchinson (Option 2): Known as a founder of modern limnology and the concept of the ecological niche, not the Indiana Dunes work.

 

• Aldo Leopold (Option 4): An American conservationist known for "A Sand County Almanac" and the concept of a "land ethic", not the Indiana Dunes succession studies.

question: The layer of earth that separates the crust from the core is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mantle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mantle is the layer of the Earth situated between the crust and the core, extending to a depth of about 2,900 km. (मेंटल — पृथ्वी की भूपर्पटी और क्रोड के बीच की परत)

 

• It is the largest layer of the Earth by volume, composed mainly of silicate rocks rich in iron and magnesium, and is divided into the upper mantle and lower mantle.

 

• The uppermost, partially molten part of the mantle (the asthenosphere) is responsible for the slow movement of tectonic plates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Earth's structure, from outermost to innermost, consists of the crust, mantle, outer core (liquid) and inner core (solid).

 

• The core is primarily composed of iron and nickel, and the inner core is solid due to immense pressure despite very high temperatures.

 

NOTE

 

• Stratosphere (Option 1): A layer of Earth's atmosphere, not a layer of the Earth's solid interior.

 

• magma layer (Option 3): Not a standard scientific term for a distinct Earth layer; magma is molten rock found within parts of the crust and mantle.

 

• country (Option 4): Not a scientific term related to Earth's internal structure.

question: Iron age is so named because during this time iron mostly replaced _________ in implements and weapons, beginning in the Middle East and South-eastern Europe.
solution_text:
The correct answer is bronze.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Iron Age is so named because, during this period, iron largely replaced bronze as the primary material for making tools, implements and weapons. (लौह युग — कांस्य का स्थान लोहे ने लिया)

 

• This transition began around 1200 BCE in the Middle East and South-eastern Europe, following the decline of major Bronze Age civilisations (the so-called "Bronze Age Collapse").

 

• Iron was preferred over bronze because iron ore was more widely available than the tin needed for bronze, and iron tools could be made harder and more durable.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In the traditional Three-Age System of archaeology, the sequence is Stone Age → Bronze Age → Iron Age, representing progressively advanced tool-making technologies.

 

• In the Indian subcontinent, iron use is generally dated from around 1500-1200 BCE onwards, associated with the later Vedic period.

 

NOTE

 

• wood (Option 1): Wood was used for tools even before the Bronze Age but is not what iron is specifically said to have "replaced" in naming this era.

 

• brass (Option 2): An alloy of copper and zinc, developed much later and not the material iron is described as replacing.

 

• stone (Option 4): Stone was replaced by bronze (giving the Bronze Age), not directly by iron in this naming convention.

question: Which country celebrates one of the famous festivals known as Paro Tschechu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhutan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Paro Tshechu is one of the most famous religious festivals of Bhutan, held annually at the Paro Dzong (Rinpung Dzong). (पारो त्शेचु महोत्सव — भूटान)

 

• The festival honours Guru Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), who is credited with introducing Buddhism to Bhutan, and features elaborate masked dances (cham) performed by monks.

 

• A highlight of the festival is the unfurling of a giant thongdrel (sacred appliqué scroll/thangka) on the final day, believed to cleanse viewers of sin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tshechu festivals ('tenth day' festivals) are held at various dzongs (fortress-monasteries) across Bhutan on dates tied to the Bhutanese lunar calendar; other well-known ones include the Thimphu Tshechu and Punakha Tshechu.

 

• Bhutan measures development through Gross National Happiness (GNH) rather than relying solely on GDP.

 

NOTE

 

• Japan (Option 1): Known for festivals such as Hanami (cherry blossom viewing), not Paro Tshechu.

 

• Thailand (Option 3): Known for festivals such as Songkran, not Paro Tshechu.

 

• Burma (Myanmar) (Option 4): Known for festivals such as Thingyan, not Paro Tshechu.
